item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-14
item.description: On 2026-11-13 two curricula were published, and together they answer a question this series has been asking for a fortnight. At the Agentic Infra OS Conference and openEuler Summit 2026 in Beijing, openEuler released an operating system built for AI agents on top of 24.03 LTS SP5 and reported, via Frost & Sullivan, that it will take 61% of China's new server-OS market in 2026 on cumulative installs expected to pass 22 million -- and that the Pakistan Higher Education Commission has released HECOS 1.0, the first national operating system outside China built on openEuler. That is the first export in this run of briefings that is a distribution rather than a filing. The same week, at CCF ChinaSoft 2026 in Tianjin on 6 November, Huawei reported that HarmonyOS coursework now reaches 650-plus universities and 800-plus courses with 460,000-plus registered student developers, on a documented chain of course, practice, exam, certification -- and that the HarmonyOS university innovation contest has entered the national discipline-competition ranking for the first time. One is a commons leaving the country as a downstream that someone else maintains; the other is a curriculum entering the university at national scale. Neither is a governance textbook, and that absence is the finding.
